newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil anti-trust body to rule on brewery deal.
newsitem.headline: Brazil anti-trust body to rule on brewery deal.

text.p: A Brazilian anti-trust body is due to rule Wednesday on whether the partnership between brewers Antarctica and Anheuser-Busch Cos. impedes competition, an official said.
The government's Administrative Economic Defence Council (Cade) began meeting early Wednesday to decide whether the joint-venture is harmful to competition in the beverage sector.

Anheuser-Busch Cos., maker of Budweiser beer, and local brewery Companhia Antarctica Paulista set up the joint-venture in 1995 to distribute Budweiser in Brazil. Under the deal, Anheuser, the world's largest brewer, also bought an equity stake in the Brazilian company.

The Cade has not taken any decision yet, but newspapers have said that it is likely that the anti-trust body's ruling will be the same as last week's ruling on another partnership between local and foreign brewers.

The Cade ordered Brazil's Brahma, the largest brewer in South America, and U.S. Miller Brewing Co. to dissolve their joint-venture within 24 months because it was found that the partnership was against the interests of competition.

Under the venture, which had been due to expire in 2010, Brahma sold and distributed Miller products in Brazil, giving its parent company Philip Morris Cos Inc. a foothold in the booming Brazilian beer market.
The council found that Miller could have entered the Brazilian market on its own.
Brahma is appealing the Cade decision.

A lawyer for Antarctica told Gazeta Mercantil financial newspaper Wednesday the Antarctica-Anheuser deal is different because the joint-venture was aimed at increasing output, creating jobs and distributing Brazilian products in the U.S. market.
"It is not possible that the interpretation will be the same," Carlos Francisco de Magalhaes was quoted as saying.

Under the venture, the Brazilian company could take advantage of Anheuser's presence in 80 countries to explore distribution opportunities in other parts of the world, contributing to improve the firm's competitiveness, Gazeta said.
After the Antarctica-Anheuser deal, the Cade will also study an agreement between Brazil's Skol and Danish brewer Carlsberg , the newspaper added. Skol is owned by Brahma.
